body: [{"streamId":"01a0d875-281e-7304-81f8-07bfba9c83dd","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskAdded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0d875-281e-7304-81f8-07bfba9c83dd\u0022,\u0022ProjectId\u0022:\u002201a0a27f-abdf-7731-84aa-d604e9bc53ca\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:\u0022odo walk follows Carvana\\u0027s result pages (page=2, page=3, and so on) until the per-pair cap is met or a page adds no new links, so a pair is no longer limited to the roughly 21 cars Carvana renders on its first page\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022For carvana, after collecting a search page\\u0027s links, the walk requests the same URL with page=N for N from 2 upward while the candidate pool is below the link pool size and the last page added at least one new canonical link, recording each page as search.txt, search-2.txt, and so on through the existing WalkRecorder naming; proven by a walk test whose fake browser serves three pages and asserts the pool contains links from all three and stops after a page adds nothing new\u0022,\u0022The pacing between pages is the existing scroll-and-dwell rhythm (ScrollInStepsAsync plus RandomDwell) and the per-pair cap is unchanged; cars.com is untouched (its two-search rule from PR #40 still holds); proven by existing walk tests passing\u0022,\u0022The README\\u0027s walk section says Carvana is paged and the summary line still counts the pair as one row; dotnet build and dotnet test succeed with zero warnings; commits are small with conventional messages, no em dashes, no AI attribution\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Bugfix\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Found by the orchestrator over CDP in Brian\\u0027s Edge on 2026-09-25 (notes/run-session-2026-09-22.md, section \\u0027Autotrader and Carvana facts\\u0027). Walk run 4 saved 21 of 21 Prius links on carvana and the run session concluded carvana\\u0027s inventory was exhausted; it is not: the same search reports 100 cars and Carvana renders about 21 cards per page, paging with a plain page=N query parameter on the same filters URL (page=2 returned 23 different /vehicle/ links). The walk\\u0027s carvana URL carries no radius, so no radius change is needed. Code: WalkPairAsync in src/Odonomics/Cli/Commands/WalkCommand.cs collects links from one page per search; WalkPairSearches (PR #40) already lets a pair have more than one search page and shares the cap across them, so model a Carvana result page as one more search in that list rather than a new loop. walk covers Autotrader as a third site, every seller type including private sellers, with the scenario\\u0027s zip, radius, minimum year, maximum mileage, and hybrid filter as search facets, so https://www.autotrader.com/cars-for-sale/used-cars/\\u003Cmake\\u003E/\\u003Cbase model slug\\u003E?zip=\\u003Czip\\u003E\\u0026searchRadius=\\u003Cradius\\u003E\\u0026startYear=\\u003Cminimum model year\\u003E\\u0026maxMileage=\\u003Cmaximum mileage\\u003E\\u0026sortBy=relevance, adding \\u0026fuelTypeGroup=HYB when the scenario model is a hybrid variant of a base model (Corolla Hybrid, Camry Hybrid, Camry Hybrid, and Insight\u0022,\u0022Detail links match /cars-for-sale/vehicle/\\u003Cdigits\\u003E and CanonicalDetailUrl strips query strings and fragments such as #purchaseConfidence so one listing yields one candidate; a search page whose text reads \\u00270 Matches\\u0027 contributes no links even though Autotrader fills it with cards of other models and years; proven by a link-collection test over a fixture cut from a recorded Autotrader search page (record one with the walk\\u0027s own recorder or from a CDP capture) and one over a zero-match page\u0022,\u0022A private-seller listing is stored with the dealer name \\u0027Private seller\\u0027 and no location, ListingQuery.MatchesExtractedVehicle applies unchanged, and odo dealer grade skips \\u0027Private seller\\u0027 rows without calling CarEdge; proven by tests\u0022,\u0022A bare odo walk visits cars.com, carvana, then autotrader; odo walk autotrader narrows to it; the ChallengeDetector and the messages, no em dashes, no AI attribution\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Feature\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Brian\\u0027s direction on 2026-09-25: Autotrader is wanted for every seller type, because private sellers list there (cars.com and carvana carry none) and because smaller dealers may list there and not on cars.com. Idea 31e7ce32 holds the history. The orchestrator verified the facets over CDP in Brian\\u0027s Edge the same morning; the details are in notes/run-session-2026-09-22.md, section \\u0027Autotrader and Carvana facts, verified by the orchestrator\\u0027: the site rewrites the URL to /cars-for-sale/\\u003Cmake\\u003E/\\u003Cmodel\\u003E/orlando-fl?... but honors every parameter; model slugs are prius, corolla, camry, insight, there is no corolla-hybrid or camry-hybrid model and a made-up slug silently returns every Toyota; hybrids are fuelTypeGroup=HYB (Corolla 2019\\u002B within 50 miles: 347 matches without, 41 with); the count text is \\u0027N Matches\\u0027; a detail page carries \\u0027VIN: ...\\u0027, \\u0027N mi\\u0027, the price, and an itemized dealer-fee block (Electronic Filing Fee, Private Tag Agency Fee, Reconditioning Fee) that a later task may capture; no bot challenge appeared in about forty loads. Code to follow: WalkSites.cs (CarsCom and Carvana records, SkippedCardTitlePattern, CanonicalDetailUrl), WalkPairSearches (PR #40) for multiple searches per pair, ListingQuery.For for the facet values, CarvanaDealers.cs and LedgerUpsertService for how a site-specific seller name is keyed, the dealer grade command for where a seller is looked up on CarEdge. Autotrader used-cars search returned 2026 model-year cards; if they prove to be new cars, reuse the New-title skip from PR #39. the carvana walk reads it from the detail page text (\\u0027Free shipping\\u0027 stores 0, \\u0027$1,590 shipping\\u0027 stores 1590, absent stores null) and the upsert keeps the latest value; other sites store null; proven by extraction and upsert tests over a fixture cut from a recorded Carvana detail page\u0022,\u0022Wherever budget, rank, and show take a posting\\u0027s price into a purchase-price figure (BudgetSolver, VehiclePricing, the rank and show renderers), the price used is asking price plus shipping fee when the fee is known; odo show prints the fee as its own line under the price, and rank --detail names it in the itemized breakdown; a null fee changes nothing; proven by tests\u0022,\u0022The README\\u0027s Carvana notes and the budget section say the shipping fee counts toward the purchase price; dotnet build and dotnet test succeed with zero warnings; commits are small with conventional messages, no em dashes, no AI attribution\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Feature\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Brian asked on 2026-09-25 whether Carvana\\u0027s shipping cost has to be taken into account now that far-away Carvana cars are in play; the orchestrator\\u0027s answer is yes, as a one-time purchase cost. Verified over CDP the same morning (notes/run-session-2026-09-22.md, section \\u0027Autotrader and Carvana facts\\u0027): every Carvana search card shows \\u0027Free shipping\\u0027 or \\u0027$290 shipping\\u0027 through \\u0027$1,590 shipping\\u0027, and a detail page (vehicle/4764388, a 2025 Prius LE) shows \\u0027$1,590 shipping | Get it Tuesday\\u0027 beside \\u0027Pickup ... Orlando, FL\\u0027, so the fee is per car and depends on the buyer\\u0027s zip; free pickup at the Orlando hub is the alternative Brian may take, which is why the fee is stored rather than baked into the price observation. Code: ListingCandidate.cs and Entities.cs (PriceObservationEntity holds the asking price history; keep the fee off it), LedgerUpsertService, the carvana detail extraction path in WalkCommand.cs, BudgetSolver.MaxPurchasePrice and VehiclePricing.cs for where price becomes a purchase figure, and the show and rank renderers (PR #35 and PR #36 added the itemized monthly breakdown and the rounding reconciliation; keep those reconciling).
